[{'number': 2555, 'title': 'fix: stop TraverseChildren from executing subcommands after --', 'body': 'Fixes #2528.\n\nProblem: with `TraverseChildren: true`, a token after the `--` delimiter that matches a subcommand name was executed as that subcommand, discarding positional arguments. For example, `./app -- literal child` invoked `child` instead of invoking the root command with positional arguments `["literal", "child"]`.\n\nChange: `Traverse` now returns the current command at `--`, so tokens after `--` are never treated as subcommands. Traversal behavior for tokens before `--` is unchanged, as is behavior when `TraverseChildren` is false. The regression was applied only in an isolated worktree. The regression proof records three executed states: the existing tests pass with that regression, the new assertion fails against the **same** regression, and the new test passes with the original production code restored. No other occurrence of the wrong form is left in the docs (`grep -n "for usage" site/content/user_guide.md` now shows only the `--help` forms).\n\nTests: `go test ./...` passes on this tree (`ok github.com/spf13/cobra 0.579s`, `doc` cached); the change is docs-only so no new test is needed.\n', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2550', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'qwen/docs-usage-hint-kubectl', 'sha': '22d609f507220af3927d1f02f2bac064d4dd9392', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-22T16:53:03Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-22T16:53:03Z'}, {'number': 2549, 'title': 'doc: state the full scope of DisableSuggestions', 'body': '## What\n\nThe `DisableSuggestions` field comment says it "disables the suggestions based on Levenshtein distance". In fact `findSuggestions` returns immediately when the field is set:\n\n```go\nfunc (c *Command) findSuggestions(arg string) string {\n\tif c.DisableSuggestions {\n\t\treturn ""\n\t}\n```\n\nwhich suppresses everything `SuggestionsFor` can emit — Levenshtein matches, **prefix matches** (`strings.HasPrefix(cmd.Name(), typedName)`), and explicit `SuggestFor` entries — not only the Levenshtein-based ones. The comment is updated to state the real scope.\n\n## Testing\n\nComment-only change; `go build ./...` and `gofmt` clean.\n\n## AI assistance\n\nAn AI agent noticed the comment-to-implementation gap in `command.go:782-784` and `:869-876`; I verified both code paths and wrote the final wording.\n', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2549', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'docs/disable-suggestions-scope', 'sha': 'c04f8f538bbb674e54e7fcac59558d8c7f399ddf', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-21T23:26:43Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-21T23:26:43Z'}, {'number': 2548, 'title': "doc: correct the 'does not modify' claim on flag-set getters", 'body': '## What\n\n`LocalFlags`, `LocalNonPersistentFlags`, `InheritedFlags` and `NonInheritedFlags` all claim "This function does not modify the flags of the current command, it\'s purpose is to return the current state." Each of them actually calls `mergePersistentFlags()` (directly, or transitively via `LocalFlags()`), and `mergePersistentFlags` does modify the command\'s flag state:\n\n```go\nfunc (c *Command) mergePersistentFlags() {\n\tc.updateParentsPflags()\n\tc.Flags().AddFlagSet(c.PersistentFlags())\n\tc.Flags().AddFlagSet(c.parentsPflags)\n}\n```\n\nSo after calling any of these getters, `c.Flags()` contains persistent flags inherited from parents — the doc comment says the opposite. This PR replaces the sentence with an accurate description of the side effect on all four functions.\n\n## Testing\n\nComment-only change. `go build ./...` and `go test ./ ./doc/` pass on go1.27.1.\n\n## AI assistance\n\nAn AI agent flagged the mismatch between the comments and `mergePersistentFlags`; I read `command.go:1694-1905` myself and verified all four call chains before writing the new wording.\n', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2548', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'docs/local-non-persistent-flags-side-effect', 'sha': 'c7f9e8cb5b0e7964ba9c42307206d56f4b00a3f4', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-21T23:26:10Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-21T23:26:10Z'}, {'number': 2546, 'title': 'chore: lint some more', 'body': 'Add a bunch more useful linters, address findings if any. Few of the added ones do at time of writing, but they add useful guards.', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2546', 'user': {'login': 'scop', 'id': 109152, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/scop', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/109152?v=4'}, 'labels': ['area/docs-generation'], 'head': {'ref': 'chore/more-linting', 'sha': '3ae0b03736a4fb0b60bad6e918669d52ea66bdc1', 'repo': {'full_name': 'scop/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-21T18:51:53Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-21T18:52:02Z'}, {'number': 2545, 'title': 'fix: skip the mousetrap when arguments are passed', 'body': 'Fixes #2544\r\n\r\n**Mousetrap**\r\n* Trap only when `len(os.Args) == 1`\r\n* A double-click passes no arguments\r\n* Explorer-started commands with arguments run\r\n\r\n**Docs**\r\n* `MousetrapHelpText`, `MousetrapDisplayDuration`: "with no arguments"\r\n\r\n**Tests**\r\n* `command_win_test.go`: double-click, explorer with arguments, not explorer, disabled\r\n* `startedByExplorer` is a package var so the test can fake the parent\r\n\r\nReal case: Programs and Features starts `UninstallString` (`app.exe uninstall --purge`) with `explorer.exe` as the parent. Today cobra prints the mousetrap, waits 5s and exits 1, so the uninstall never runs.', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2545', 'user': {'login': 'danikpfive', 'id': 293805840, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/danikpfive', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/293805840?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'mousetrap-skip-when-args', 'sha': 'd2d6026c4cd91bd25ea8a44e95b3f5313ef71b5b', 'repo': {'full_name': 'danikpfive/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-21T16:07:56Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-21T16:08:51Z'}, {'number': 2543, 'title': 'docs: correct the MarkFlagsRequiredTogether comment', 'body': '### Summary\n\nThe doc comment on `MarkFlagsRequiredTogether` says Cobra errors "if the command is invoked with a subset (but not all) of the given flags". A subset includes the empty set, and invoking with none of the group flags is explicitly *not* an error — the validator skips a group when every flag in it is unset.\n\n`flag_groups.go:155`:\n\n```go\nif len(unset) == len(flagnameAndStatus) || len(unset) == 0 {\n    continue\n}\n```\n\nso nothing is reported when `unset` holds all of the group\'s flags. The message Cobra returns is already phrased correctly: "if any flags in the group [%v] are set they must all be set; missing %v" (line 161). Only the comment is off, and it is the text that shows up in godoc for one of the most-used group helpers.\n\n### Changes\n\n`MarkFlagsRequiredTogether`\'s comment now reads: errors when *at least one, but not all* of the flags are given, states that passing none is allowed, and points at `MarkFlagsOneRequired` (line 49) for the case where at least one is mandatory. No behaviour change; no other files touched.\n\n### Related issues\n\nNone. #1775 and #2502 change the group implementation and flag-name handling; this only fixes the description.\n\n### Testing\n\n* `go test . -run TestValidateFlagGroups -count=1` -> `ok github.com/spf13/cobra`\n* `go build ./...` clean, `gofmt -l .` -> no output\n\nThe behaviour the new comment describes is already covered by the existing table test: `flag_groups_test.go:59-62` registers a required group `a b` and passes no flags at all, expecting no error, while `flag_groups_test.go:63-67` sets only `--a=foo` and expects the "they must all be set" error.\n\n### AI assistance\n\nAn AI coding agent compared the validator against the comment and drafted the wording; a human reviewed it and is responsible for the contribution (CLA signed).\n', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2543', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'docs/required-together-comment', 'sha': '7dc81fef3f4468a38456185d1a1f575b9cd0e8ca', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-21T02:55:23Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-21T02:55:23Z'}, {'number': 2542, 'title': 'docs: avoid writing generated docs straight into /tmp in the examples', 'body': '### Summary\n\n`doc.GenMarkdownTree(cmd, "/tmp")` and its siblings appear as "the example" on all four docgen pages and in `ExampleGenManTree`. Writing generated docs straight into `/tmp` is unsafe: as reported in #759, `/tmp` is world-writable, so another user can plant `/tmp/test.md` as a symlink and have the generated document follow it — worst case when the generator runs as root.\n\nThis changes the examples to create a private directory with `os.MkdirTemp` and clean it up afterwards, which is also what the package\'s own tests already do (`doc/md_docs_test.go:96`).\n\nFixes #759.\n\n### Changes\n\n* `site/content/docgen/md.md`, `rest.md`, `yaml.md`, `man.md`: the import block gains `"os"`, the fixed output path becomes a temp directory, and the follow-up sentence now names the file inside it ("a Markdown document `test.md` inside that directory") instead of `/tmp/test.md`.\n* `doc/man_examples_test.go`: `ExampleGenManTree` uses `os.MkdirTemp` + `cobra.CheckErr` and removes the directory on return, so the tested example matches the docs page.\n\n### Testing\n\n* `go build ./...` clean, `go test ./... -count=1` -> `ok github.com/spf13/cobra`, `ok github.com/spf13/cobra/doc`\n* `gofmt -l doc/` -> no output\n* To check that the documentation snippets are not just plausible-looking, a temporary test in `package doc_test` (removed before committing) ran the exact new code from `md.md` and `man.md`: it produced `test.md` and `test.3` inside the temp directory and passed.\n\nDocs and an example test only; no library behaviour changes.\n\n### AI assistance\n\nAn AI coding agent prepared the edits and ran the checks above; a human reviewed them and is responsible for the contribution (CLA signed).\n', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2542', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'labels': ['area/docs-generation'], 'head': {'ref': 'docs/safe-tempdir-examples', 'sha': 'ef7b02e1d5cfa9597e1cfbc566d046b3e705caf9', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': '2026-10-19T17:07:28Z'}, {'number': 2538, 'title': 'doc: state the runnability requirement of IsAvailableCommand', 'body': '### What\n\n`IsAvailableCommand`\'s doc comment claims it "includes all non deprecated/hidden commands". The function returns `false` for two further cases.\n\n### Why\n\n`command.go:1607-1621`:\n\n```go\nfunc (c *Command) IsAvailableCommand() bool {\n\tif len(c.Deprecated) != 0 || c.Hidden {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\tif c.HasParent() && c.Parent().helpCommand == c {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\tif c.Runnable() || c.HasAvailableSubCommands() {\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\n\treturn false\n}\n```\n\nA command that is neither deprecated nor hidden still returns `false` when it is not runnable (`Runnable()` is `c.Run != nil || c.RunE != nil`, `command.go:1596-1598`) and has no available subcommands — e.g. a bare `&Command{Use: "child"}` placeholder — and the default `help` command is excluded explicitly by the second check. So "all non deprecated/hidden commands" over-promises in two distinct ways, and the trailing `return false` makes it clear the third condition is a requirement rather than an oversight.\n\nThis matters because the function gates user-visible output: the help/usage templates (`command.go:1285`, `:1378`, `:1953-1959`, `:1997-2013`), shell completion (`completions.go:521`, `bash_completions.go:450`, `:654`) and the doc generators (`doc/md_docs.go:102`, `:135`, `doc/man_docs.go:54`, `:234`). A reader who trusts the parenthetical will conclude that a non-runnable, non-hidden command appears in those lists, and it does not.\n\nThe neighbouring doc for `HasAvailableSubCommands` (`command.go:1660-1661`) already states its condition precisely ("available sub commands that can be shown in help output"), so this comment is the outlier.\n\n### Change\n\nExtend the parenthetical to name the runnability requirement. Comment-only; no behavior change.\n\n### Testing\n\n`gofmt`-neutral (a line-comment block, no code or alignment touched) and no behavior change, so `go test ./...` was not re-run. I could not execute `make all` in my environment; everything above is from reading `command.go` and its call sites at `main`.\n\n### Relation to my other open PRs\n\nIndependent of #2536 (`command.go`, a `DisplayName` comment far from this one), #2534 (`site/content/user_guide.md`), #2533 (`doc/` generator comments) and #2537 (`completions.go`).\n\n<sub>Submitted with AI assistance; the doc/code discrepancy was verified line by line against `command.go` and its call sites before opening.</sub>\n', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2538', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'doc/is-available-command-scope', 'sha': 'bb9e287274f0245218a0f767d32681751ac5b200', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-19T03:35:41Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-19T03:35:41Z'}, {'number': 2537, 'title': 'doc: correct when InitDefaultCompletionCmd skips the completion command', 'body': '### What\n\n`InitDefaultCompletionCmd`\'s doc comment says the function "will do nothing if ... c has no subcommands (to avoid creating one)". The code no longer works that way.\n\n### Why\n\nBefore #1559 the function did return early on `!c.HasSubCommands()`. That check was removed when the feature changed: the completion command is now created and `c.AddCommand(completionCmd)` is called unconditionally (`completions.go:783`), and only afterwards, at `completions.go:785-799`, it is removed again **when it is neither being executed nor being completed**:\n\n```go\nif !hasSubCommands {\n    // If the \'completion\' command will be the only sub-command,\n    // we only create it if it is actually being called.\n    ...\n    subCmd, cmdArgs, err := c.Find(args)\n    if err != nil || subCmd.Name() != compCmdName &&\n        (subCmd.Name() != ShellCompRequestCmd || len(cmdArgs) <= 1 || cmdArgs[0] != compCmdName) {\n        c.RemoveCommand(completionCmd)\n        return\n    }\n}\n```\n\n`git show` of #1559 confirms the early return was replaced by this block while bullets 1-3 of the comment were left untouched, so bullet 2 is the part that went stale. The behavior is deliberate and test-pinned — `completions_test.go:2468` "Test that when there are no sub-commands, the completion command is not created if it is not called directly." and `completions_test.go:2477` "...is created when it is called directly." It also explains why the function takes variadic `args ...string` at all, which the comment never mentions.\n\nAs written, the comment tells a reader that a subcommand-less command never gets a `completion` command, which is exactly the case the `args` parameter exists to special-case.\n\n### Change\n\nReword bullet 2 only. Bullets 1 and 3 match the early returns at `completions.go:749-751` and `:753-758` and are left as is. Comment-only; no behavior change.\n\n### Testing\n\n`gofmt`-neutral (a line-comment block, no code or alignment touched) and no behavior change, so `go test ./...` was not re-run. I could not run `make all` in my environment; the claim above is from reading `completions.go` and `completions_test.go` at `main`.\n\n### Relation to my other open PRs\n\n#2536 and #2534 touch `command.go` and `site/content/user_guide.md` respectively, #2533 the generator doc comments — none of them touch `completions.go`, so this hunk is independent.\n\n<sub>Submitted with AI assistance; the doc/code discrepancy was verified line by line against `completions.go`, `completions_test.go` and the original #1559 diff before opening.</sub>\n', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2537', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'doc/init-default-completion-cmd-no-subcommands', 'sha': 'f31c677779e809dfbdf1bdbe9b45fe18d8fef585', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-19T03:34:44Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-19T03:34:44Z'}, {'number': 2536, 'title': 'doc: fix CommandDisplayNameAnnotation typo in DisplayName', 'body': "**What this PR does**\n\n`command.go:1473` — the doc comment on `DisplayName` — refers to\n`CommandDisplayNameAnnoation`. The constant is spelled\n`CommandDisplayNameAnnotation` (`command.go:35`), and the function body two\nlines below reads precisely that key:\n\n```go\nfunc (c *Command) DisplayName() string {\n\tif displayName, ok := c.Annotations[CommandDisplayNameAnnotation]; ok {\n```\n\nSo the only place a reader is told *which* annotation to set is the one place\nwhere the name is misspelled.\n\n**Why it matters**\n\nThe misspelling is not cosmetic here: the identifier in the comment does not\nexist, so a reader who copies it gets a compile error, and `site/content/user_guide.md:840,857`\nalready documents the correctly-spelled `cobra.CommandDisplayNameAnnotation`.\nGrep confirms `command.go:1473` is the only occurrence of `Annoation` in the\nwhole repository — this is the last stale spot.\n\nComment-only change; no behaviour touched. I left the surrounding sentence\nuntouched on purpose (it reads a little telegraphically, but rewording prose\nthat isn't wrong felt like unnecessary churn — say the word if you'd rather it\nalso be smoothed out).\n\n**Testing**\n\nOne character-class fix inside a `//` comment line, so there is nothing to\ncompile or run: the token is not referenced by any code, and `go test ./...` /\n`make all` output is unaffected by definition. Note that in any case this\nsession has no Go toolchain available (shell commands are blocked by its\nsandbox), so no build or test was executed — the claims above were checked by\nreading `command.go` at `main` (`adbc881`) and by a repository-wide grep for\nboth spellings.\n\n**Relation to open PRs**\n\nSearched open PRs for `Annoation` and for `DisplayName annotation`: no hits. My\nown open PRs here (#2529, #2530, #2533, #2534) do not touch `command.go` around\n`DisplayName` — #2534 edits the `Args` doc comment and #2533 edits `doc/*_docs.go`.\n", 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2536', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'doc/display-name-annotation-spelling', 'sha': 'efae219020e63bba5b9a8d4360687643d7544b75', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-18T21:33:23Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-18T21:33:23Z'}, {'number': 2535, 'title': 'Fix: inherit parent local flags passed before subcommand (#2311)', 'body': "## What this PR does / Why we need it\n\nFixes https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/2311\n\nA flag that is valid on a parent command (e.g. `kubectl create -o`) was not\ninherited by the resolved subcommand, because only persistent flags are merged\ninto it. Running `create -o yaml svc` failed with `unknown shorthand flag: 'o'\nin -o` even though `-o` is a valid flag of the `create` group.\n\nThe fix retries parsing in `execute()` after merging the parent's local flags\ninto the resolved command, but only when a flag passed *before* the subcommand\nname is a local flag of a parent. This is order-sensitive, so a flag passed\n*after* the subcommand still errors as before (`TestChildFlagWithParentLocalFlag`\nis preserved).\n\n## Which issue(s) does this PR fix?\n\nFixes #2311\n\n## Special notes for your reviewer\n\n- `command.go`: added retry in `execute()` + new helper `inheritParentLocalFlagsIfPreceding()`\n- `command_test.go`: added regression test `TestParentLocalFlagWithSubcommand`\n- Full test suite: 261 PASS / 0 FAIL\n\nI will sign the CLA when prompted.\n", 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2535', 'user': {'login': 'xingzihai', 'id': 87858694, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/xingzihai', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/87858694?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'fix/issue-2311-subcommand-flag-parsing', 'sha': 'c07539e4c515b1a65f8ca3eae99c7f0354e0953b', 'repo': {'full_name': 'xingzihai/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-18T03:05:25Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-18T03:05:53Z'}, {'number': 2534, 'title': 'docs: clarify default Args behavior when Args is nil', 'body': "**What this PR does**\n\nCorrects the user guide's description of the default argument validation when a command's `Args` field is `nil`.\n\nThe guide stated:\n\n> If `Args` is undefined or `nil`, it defaults to `ArbitraryArgs`.\n\nThat is not the effective default. When `Args` is `nil`, `Command.Find` runs `legacyArgs` (see `command.go` `Find` -> `legacyArgs(commandFound, ...)`), not `ArbitraryArgs`. `legacyArgs` has the following behaviour (documented in `args.go`):\n\n- root commands with no subcommands can take arbitrary arguments\n- root commands with subcommands will do subcommand validity checking\n- subcommands will always accept arbitrary arguments\n\nSo a root command that has subcommands will report an error for a positional argument that is not a known subcommand, which `ArbitraryArgs` (never returns an error) would not.\n\n**Why we need it**\n\nThe previous wording could mislead users into thinking that leaving `Args` unset always accepts any positional arguments, when in fact the root-with-subcommands case enforces subcommand validity.\n\n**Which issue this PR fixes**\n\nDocumentation accuracy fix; no open issue filed.\n\n**Special notes for your reviewer**\n\nDocs-only change to a single sentence in `site/content/user_guide.md`. The new wording is taken directly from the `legacyArgs` behaviour described in `args.go` and applied at the `command.go` `Find` call site. Verified against the source at the current base commit; no code paths are modified.\n\n```release-note\nnone\n```\n", 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2534', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'doc-args-default-legacyargs', 'sha': '1ad23adfaa009f8a2113219d9f3479231b714e21', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-17T17:42:45Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-17T17:42:45Z'}, {'number': 2533, 'title': 'doc: correct output file extension in generator doc comments', 'body': '**What this PR does**\n\nThe doc comments on three of the four tree-generating functions in the `doc` package claim\nthat, in the collision example, "help output will be in the file `cmd-sub-third.1`". That\n`.1` extension was copied from the man-page generator, but these functions never write a\n`.1` file:\n\n- `GenMarkdownTree` (`doc/md_docs.go`) writes `... + markdownExtension` where `markdownExtension = ".md"` → `.md`\n- `GenReSTTree` (`doc/rest_docs.go`) writes `... + ".rst"` → `.rst`\n- `GenYamlTree` (`doc/yaml_docs.go`) writes `... + ".yaml"` → `.yaml`\n\nOnly `man_docs.go` legitimately emits `basename + "." + section` (i.e. `.1`), so its\ncomment is correct and is left untouched.\n\nThis updates each of the three comments to name the extension that generator actually\nproduces. Comment-only change; no behavior touched.\n\n**Why it matters**\n\nThe comment is telling the reader what file the output ends up in, and `.1` (a man-page\nsuffix) is misleading in the markdown/reST/YAML docs.\n\n**Testing**\n\nComment-only, so nothing to build or run (no Go toolchain in this environment either). The\nextension claims above were checked directly against the `basename :=` lines in each file at\n`main` (`adbc881`).\n\n**Relation to open PRs**\n\nI checked the open PRs that touch these same files; none edits this comment:\n- #2470 (sanitize path separators) edits the `basename`/`link` code and `util.go`, plus tests — disjoint hunks from these comment lines.\n- #2515 (trailing newline) and #2503 (hidden/deprecated YAML flags) also edit generator bodies, not the doc comment.\n\nHappy to rebase if any of those land first and shift context.\n', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2533', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'labels': ['area/docs-generation'], 'head': {'ref': 'doc-comment-output-ext', 'sha': '13981f45962d15f3e51f4c76284637a0fb82b939', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-17T17:27:05Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-17T17:27:15Z'}, {'number': 2532, 'title': "command: stop Traverse at `--` so a positional isn't run as a subcommand", 'body': '## Bug (fixes #2528)\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, the long-flag branch of `Command.Traverse` matched a bare `--` as a flag that "takes a value":\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--") && !strings.Contains(arg, "="):\n    inFlag = !hasNoOptDefVal(arg[2:], c.Flags())\n    flags = append(flags, arg)\n    continue\n```\n\n`arg[2:]` is `""`, no flag by that name exists, so `inFlag = true`. The next positional is consumed as that flag\'s "value" and the following positional happens to match a subcommand — so the child handler runs, the first post-`--` positional is silently dropped, and the parent\'s positionals never reach any command.\n\nReproduction from the issue:\n\n```go\nroot := &cobra.Command{Use:"app", TraverseChildren:true, Args:cobra.ArbitraryArgs,\n    Run: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string){ fmt.Printf("root called with %q\\\\n", args) }}\nroot.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{Use:"child",\n    Run: func(*cobra.Command, []string){ fmt.Println("child called") }})\nroot.Execute()\n```\n\n```\n$ ./app -- literal child\nchild called                 # bug: wrong handler, "literal" lost\n$ # expected:\nroot called with ["literal" "child"]\n```\n\nThe default (non-traverse) `stripFlags` path already stops command discovery on `--`.\n\n## Fix\n\nMirror that behaviour. When `Traverse` sees a bare `--`:\n\n1. Parse any flags accumulated so far on the current command.\n2. Return the current command along with the remaining args starting at the delimiter, so a downstream parser sees the exact slice it would have gotten without `TraverseChildren`.\n\n## Test\n\n`TestTraverseStopsAtEndOfFlags` covers two cases:\n\n- `[]string{"--", "literal", "child"}` → traversal stays on root, remaining is unchanged.\n- `[]string{"--", "child"}` → traversal stays on root, remaining is unchanged.\n\n`go test ./...` is green.', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2532', 'user': {'login': 'piyush295', 'id': 126451870, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/piyush295', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/126451870?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'fix/traverse-stop-at-double-dash', 'sha': '944515dee56e0d7a7cc40bd772660adda0555f9c', 'repo': {'full_name': 'piyush295/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-16T05:15:32Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-16T09:26:29Z'}, {'number': 2531, 'title': 'fix: stop command traversal at --', 'body': 'Closes #2528.\n\nWhen `TraverseChildren` sees `--`, it currently handles it as a long flag and treats the next positional token as a flag value. A later token matching a child command can then dispatch to that child and drop the positional arguments.\n\nStop command discovery at `--` and leave the full argument list for the selected command to parse. Add end-to-end regressions for `-- literal child` and `-- child`.\n\nVerification:\n- `go test ./... -count=1`\n- `go vet ./...`\n- `gofmt` check on the changed files\n\nAssisted by Codex (GPT-6).', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2531', 'user': {'login': 'dannyward630', 'id': 71604164, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/dannyward630', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/71604164?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'fix/traverse-children-dash', 'sha': 'a50cd16c7acc642db322e6b8a6ee92826e4cb6d6', 'repo': {'full_name': 'dannyward630/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-15T22:47:16Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-15T22:47:25Z'}, {'number': 2530, 'title': 'fix: stop Traverse command discovery at bare --', 'body': '## Description\n\nFixes #2528.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, `Command.Traverse` treated a bare `--` as a long flag with an empty name (`arg[2:] == ""`). The next token was consumed as that flag\'s value, then command discovery resumed, so `./app -- literal child` could execute `child` and drop `literal`.\n\n`stripFlags` / `Find` already stop at `--`. Traverse now does the same: when it sees a bare `--` (and is not already collecting a flag value), it returns the current command with the full args for that level so `Execute` parses flags once and keeps later tokens as positionals.\n\n## Checklist\n\n- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).\n- [x] The code has adequate tests for the new feature / bug.\n- [x] Tests pass: `go test -run TestTraverse .`\n\n## Testing\n\n- New: `TestTraverseBareDoubleDashStopsCommandDiscovery` (`-- literal child`, `-- child`, and plain `child` controls).\n- Existing `TestTraverse*` suite passed locally.\n\n## AI assistance\n\nAI tools helped draft the patch, tests, and PR text. I reviewed the change, ran the tests above, and take responsibility for the contents.', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2530', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'fix/2528-traverse-bare-double-dash', 'sha': '9ff16b117ce6b07eec5d0249f52e6222c0dfa929', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-15T19:26:55Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-16T06:01:38Z'}, {'number': 2529, 'title': 'fix: do not apply stateful flags twice during shell completion', 'body': '## Description\n\nFixes #2527.\n\n`getCompletions` probed whether flag completion should stop (interspersed off or a prior `--`) by calling `ParseFlags` on `finalArgs` plus a trailing `"--"`, then called `ParseFlags(finalArgs)` again for the real values. Stateful pflag types (`StringArray`, `StringSlice`, `Count`) append or increment on every `Parse`, so a single `__complete` request applied each occurrence twice. Scalar flags hid the bug because assigning the same value twice looks identical.\n\nThis change keeps the same NArg comparison, but runs the probe with `ParseAll` and a no-op setter so flag values are not applied. The authoritative `ParseFlags(finalArgs)` then applies each occurrence once. The probe also copies `finalArgs` before appending `"--"`, so a shared `os.Args` backing array is not mutated (same class of issue as #2257).\n\n## Checklist\n\n- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).\n- [x] The code has adequate tests for the new feature / bug.\n- [x] Tests pass.`go test -run \'TestCompletionDoesNotDoubleApplyStatefulFlags|TestFlagCompletionWithNotInterspersedArgs|TestCompletionDoesNotMutateOsArgs|TestFlagNameCompletionRepeat|Test.*Completion\' .`\n\n## Testing\n\n- New regression: `TestCompletionDoesNotDoubleApplyStatefulFlags` (`--tag` / `--slice` / `-v` through `__complete`).\n- Existing: `TestFlagCompletionWithNotInterspersedArgs`, `TestCompletionDoesNotMutateOsArgs`, and the broader `Test.*Completion` set — all passed locally.\n- Manual repro from #2527: `./app __complete --tag one -v \'\'` now prints `tags=["one"] verbose=1` instead of duplicated values.\n\n## AI assistance\n\nAI tools helped draft the patch, tests, and PR text. I reviewed the change, ran the tests above, and take responsibility for the contents.', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2529', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/ump45nose', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/52391318?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'fix/2527-completion-double-parse-flags', 'sha': '665103c1eb751dd8ff8433170383f08369030506', 'repo': {'full_name': 'ump45nose/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-15T19:24:56Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-22T08:07:02Z'}, {'number': 2526, 'title': 'Fix zsh completion prefixes for flag values containing equals signs', 'body': 'Fix the zsh completion prefix for flag values containing additional equals signs. The current `-.*=` match can include part of a `key=value` value or a hyphen inside a separate value, making zsh duplicate text or reject a valid completion.\n\nNormalize shell quoting, match only at the start of the flag, and stop at the first `=`. Add a generated-script regression for long/short flags, combined key/value pairs, quoted and escaped flags, ordinary values, and hyphens inside separate values.\n\nAddresses the zsh case in #2309. The Fish fix in #2523 and the later Bash report have separate scope.\n\nRecorded validation on Linux, Go 1.24.13 and zsh 5.9 at base `adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e`:\n\n- Focused regression: six baseline failures, all 15 cases passing after the revised fix.\n- Real zsh ZLE completion: 14 supported cases pass, including the reported duplication with substring matching enabled; the same 14 cases pass with `GenZshCompletionNoDesc`.\n- Six native `NoSpace` controls pass, including whole-token quoted/escaped flags.\n- `go test -count=1 -json ./...`: 445 passing test/subtest events across two packages.\n- Recorded race, vet, build, make-all and lint checks pass.\n\nThese checks overlap. Unfinished quotes and spaces inside values are outside this patch. Without `NoSpace`, the existing suffix handling can insert a space inside a quoted value; the quoted key/value case now reaches that existing problem instead of producing no completion. macOS, Windows and the older-Go matrix were not tested. No new tests were run for this publication.', 'state': 'open', 'draft': True, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2526', 'user': {'login': 'hafizahmedzia', 'id': 246515321, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/hafizahmedzia', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/246515321?v=4'}, 'head': {'ref': 'fix-2309-zsh-equals-prefix', 'sha': '4c21d45113e830ac6866463ce6d1ae797ab627de', 'repo': {'full_name': 'hafizahmedzia/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-15T00:56:40Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-15T00:58:26Z'}, {'number': 2523, 'title': 'fix: avoid duplicating values in fish completion', 'body': 'The fish completion script matches a hyphen anywhere in the current token\nand includes everything through the last `=` in the flag prefix. This can\nduplicate part of the value returned by the completion callback:\n\n- `--selector=app=w` produces `--selector=app=app=web` instead of `--selector=app=web`.\n- `-s app-name=w` produces `-name=app-name=web` instead of `app-name=web`.\n\nMatch the flag only at the start of the token and stop at the first `=`.\nUse the unescaped token so quotes do not hide the flag from the anchored\npattern.\n\nAdd regression tests that run the generated script in fish with a fixed\ncompletion backend, and install fish in the Ubuntu / Go 1.24 CI job.\nA standalone Cobra reproducer is included in `testdata/fish-prefix`.\n\n## Test plan\n\n- All 27 adapter cases pass with fish 3.6.0 and 4.0.2; 14 fail on the original code.\n- The standalone CLI passes all 15 checks after the fix; 9 fail before it.\n- `make all` passes on Linux with Go 1.27.1.\n\nSimilar symptoms are reported for zsh and bash in #2309. This PR only fixes\nfish prefix handling.\n', 'state': 'open', 'draft': False, 'merged': False, 'html_url': 'https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/2523', 'user': {'login': 'U-S-jun', 'id': 157643778, 'profile_url': 'https://github.com/U-S-jun', 'avatar_url': 'https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/157643778?v=4'}, 'labels': ['area/github'], 'head': {'ref': 'fix/fish-completion-flag-prefix', 'sha': '3b93dc81aa02071d14c0f1a7481fda77a980d0a7', 'repo': {'full_name': 'U-S-jun/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'base': {'ref': 'main', 'sha': 'adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e', 'repo': {'full_name': 'spf13/cobra', 'description': 'A Commander for modern Go CLI interactions'}}, 'created_at': '2026-10-07T21:13:41Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-07T21:13:58Z'}, {'number': 2522, 'title': 'fix: render man page flags as tagged paragraphs', 'body': "Closes #2520\n\n`manPrintFlags` now writes the flag usage as a go-md2man definition list (`: usage`), which renders as `.TP`. gh uses the same form in its copy of the generator.\n\nA definition list alone isn't enough, because go-md2man still reads the usage as Markdown. It turns a usage line starting with `- `, `* `, `+ ` or `1. ` into a list and indents all following flags by 2 instead of 7. A blank line in the usage ends the definition, and the next paragraph loses its indent. The fix escapes these markers at the start of each line and indents the following lines by four spaces.\n\nThe escaping also fixes an existing bug. Until now, a usage line starting with `#` turned into a section heading, and all following flags ended up under it.\n\n`TestGenManFlagsAsTaggedParagraphs` covers these cases. `TestManPrintFlagsHidesShortDeprecated` now expects the definition list instead of the tab-indented line.\n\nI built docker, hugo, restic, caddy and helm against this branch and generated their man pages. Every flag now renders as `.TP`. The text of the pages is unchanged, only the flag layout differs.\n\nrestic's `restic-backup.1`, before and after (`MANWIDTH=80`):\n\n```\n     --exclude-caches[=false]      excludes cache directories that  are  marked\n     with  a  CACHEDIR.TAG file. ### Commit: `adbc881` — fix: resolve macOS test link failure and update lint rules (#2429)

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| **Author** | Shudhanshu Singh (`SudhanshuMatrix`) |
| **Date** | 2026-07-11 |
| **Changes** | 3 files changed, +22 / -2 |

---

### Changes:

**1. `.github/workflows/test.yml`** — Added a CI environment variable `GO_TEST_FLAGS` that forces external linking (`-ldflags=-linkmode=external`) on macOS for Go versions below 1.24. This resolves a macOS test linking failure where compiled binaries require an `LC_UUID` load command, which Go < 1.24 doesn't write natively.

**2. `.golangci.yml`** — Updated lint configuration:
- Enabled `warn-unused: true` for linters.
- Added rules to suppress `goconst` warnings for common strings like `true`, `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, and `powershell`.
- Added a rule to allow unused `//nolint:staticcheck` directives in test files (to avoid build failures across different Go/staticcheck versions in the test matrix).

**3. `Makefile`** — Updated the `test` and `richtest` targets to pass the `GO_TEST_FLAGS` environment variable to `go test` and `richgo test`, enabling the macOS linking workaround when running tests locally.

```go
// ExactArgs returns an error if there are not exactly n args.
func ExactArgs(n int) PositionalArgs {
	return func(cmd *Command, args []string) error {
		if len(args) != n {
			return fmt.Errorf("accepts %d arg(s), received %d", n, len(args))
		}
		return nil
	}
}
```

### How it works:

- **`ExactArgs(n int)`** is a higher-order function that takes an integer `n` and returns a `PositionalArgs` function (which itself is a `func(cmd *Command, args []string) error`).
- The returned closure checks whether the number of positional arguments exactly matches `n`. If it doesn't, it returns an error like `"accepts 2 arg(s), received 1"`.
- It's designed to be used as the `Args` field on a `cobra.Command`, for example:
  ```go
  cmd := &cobra.Command{
      Use:  "mycmd",
      Args: cobra.ExactArgs(2),
      Run:  func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) { ... },
  }
  ```

The file also contains related argument validators like `NoArgs`, `MinimumNArgs`, `MaximumNArgs`, `RangeArgs`, `ArbitraryArgs`, `OnlyValidArgs`, and `MatchAll`.

Here's a summary of commit `adbc881` in `spf13/cobra`:

**Title:** fix: resolve macOS test link failure and update lint rules (#2429)

**Author:** Shudhanshu Singh (SudhanshuMatrix), committed on July 11, 2026.

---

### Changes (3 files, +22/-2):

1. **`.github/workflows/test.yml`** — Added a CI environment variable `GO_TEST_FLAGS` that passes `-ldflags=-linkmode=external` on macOS when using Go versions < 1.24. This fixes test linking failures on macOS runners, which require compiled binaries to contain an `LC_UUID` load command. Go 1.24+ handles this natively; older versions need external linking via the system linker.

2. **`.golangci.yml`** — Updated lint rules:
   - Enables `warn-unused` for linter directives.
   - Suppresses `goconst` warnings in test files and for certain string literals (`true`, `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `powershell`).
   - Allows unused `//nolint:staticcheck` directives in test files to avoid build failures across different Go/staticcheck versions in the test matrix.

3. **`Makefile`** — Modified the `test` and `richtest` targets to inject the `$(GO_TEST_FLAGS)` variable into `go test` and `richgo test` commands, so the macOS linking workaround is applied automatically.

I drafted a short page (proposed `site/content/architecture.md`, draft below) mapping the files and the `Execute()` flow. Would you take it as a PR? Happy to close if not.\n\nDisclosure: I maintain RepoLens, a docs tool, and used it (v1.15.2) for the first draft; everything was checked against the source by hand.\n\n<details><summary>Draft site/content/architecture.md</summary>\n\n# Architecture (for contributors)\n\nAll of Cobra is one Go package in the repo root; `doc/` is a separate package that generates man/markdown/rst/yaml docs. Dependencies: `spf13/pflag` (flags), `inconshreveable/mousetrap` (Windows Explorer detection) and `cpuguy83/go-md2man` (for `doc/`).\n\n| File | What it holds |\n|---|---|\n| `command.go` (~2,100 lines) | `Command`: tree building, `Execute`/`ExecuteC`, `Find`/`Traverse`, flag parsing, hooks, help/usage/version. |\n| `cobra.go` | Package globals and template functions, `OnInitialize`, `EnableCommandSorting`, etc. |\n| `args.go` | Positional-arg validators (`NoArgs`, `ExactArgs`, `MatchAll`, …). |\n| `flag_groups.go` | `MarkFlagsRequiredTogether`, `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive`, `MarkFlagsOneRequired`. |\n| `completions.go` (~1,000) | The hidden `__complete` command, `ValidArgsFunction`, and the default `completion` command. |\n| `bash_completions*.go`, `zsh_`, `fish_`, `powershell_completions.go` | Shell-specific completion script generators. |\n| `active_help.go` | Active Help messages shown during completion. |\n| `command_win.go` / `command_notwin.go` | Platform-specific pre-exec (mousetrap). |\n\n## How `Execute()` runs\n1. `Execute()` calls `ExecuteC()` on the root, which adds the default help and completion commands (`InitDefaultHelpCmd`, `InitDefaultCompletionCmd`).\n2. Here's a summary of **spf13/cobra#2555**:

---

### Title
**fix: stop TraverseChildren from executing subcommands after `--`**

### Background
Fixes issue [#2528](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/2528). When `TraverseChildren: true` was set, a token appearing after the `--` delimiter that matched a subcommand name would be incorrectly executed as that subcommand, rather than being treated as a positional argument.

For example, `./app -- literal child` would incorrectly invoke the `child` subcommand instead of the root command with `["literal", "child"]` as positional arguments.

### Change
The `Traverse` method now returns the **current command** at `--`, so tokens after `--` are never treated as subcommands. Tokens before `--` are unaffected, and behavior when `TraverseChildren` is false remains unchanged.

### Details
- **Author**: [johnhldiver-beep](https://github.com/johnhldiver-beep)
- **Status**: Open (not merged)
- **Changes**: +69 lines across 2 files (including 3 new tests in `command_test.go`)
- **Verification**: `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` both pass
- **Mergeable state**: Blocked

+func TestTraverseWithDashDashDelimiter(t *testing.T) {
+	rootCmd := &Command{Use: "root", TraverseChildren: true, Args: ArbitraryArgs}
+
+	childCmd := &Command{Use: "child"}
+	rootCmd.AddCommand(childCmd)
+
+	// Tokens after "--", including one that matches a subcommand name,
+	// must be returned as positional args of the root command.
+	c, args, err := rootCmd.Traverse([]string{"--", "literal", "child"})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("Unexpected error: %v", err)
+	}
+	if c != rootCmd {
+		t.Errorf("Expected command: %q, got %q", rootCmd.Name(), c.Name())
+	}
+	if len(args) != 3 || args[0] != "--" || args[1] != "literal" || args[2] != "child" {
+		t.Errorf("Wrong args: %v", args)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestTraverseWithDashDashDelimiterExecutesRoot(t *testing.T) {
+	rootCmd := &Command{Use: "root", TraverseChildren: true, Args: ArbitraryArgs}
+
+	var rootArgs []string
+	childRan := false
+	rootCmd.Run = func(cmd *Command, args []string) {
+		rootArgs = args
+	}
+	childCmd := &Command{Use: "child", Run: func(cmd *Command, args []string) {
+		childRan = true
+	}}
+	rootCmd.AddCommand(childCmd)
+
+	rootCmd.SetArgs([]string{"--", "literal", "child"})
+	if err := rootCmd.Execute(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("Unexpected error: %v", err)
+	}
+	if childRan {
+		t.Error("Child command should not have been executed")
+	}
+	if len(rootArgs) != 2 || rootArgs[0] != "literal" || rootArgs[1] != "child" {
+		t.Errorf("Wrong root args: %v", rootArgs)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestTraverseWithFlagsBeforeDashDashDelimiter(t *testing.T) {
+	rootCmd := &Command{Use: "root", TraverseChildren: true, Args: ArbitraryArgs}
+	rootCmd.Flags().String("str", "", "")
+
+	childCmd := &Command{Use: "child"}
+	rootCmd.AddCommand(childCmd)
+
+	// Flags before "--" keep their normal traversal behavior.
+	c, args, err := rootCmd.Traverse([]string{"--str", "ok", "--", "child"})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("Unexpected error: %v", err)
+	}
+	if c != rootCmd {
+		t.Errorf("Expected command: %q, got %q", rootCmd.Name(), c.Name())
+	}
+	if len(args) != 4 || args[0] != "--str" || args[1] != "ok" || args[2] != "--" || args[3] != "child" {
+		t.Errorf("Wrong args: %v", args)
+	}
+}
+

{'issues': [{'number': 2547, 'title': 'Docs: contributor architecture overview for the `cobra` package', 'body': "The package is flat (all in the repo root), so it isn't obvious where things live. I drafted a short page (proposed `site/content/architecture.md`, draft below) mapping the files and the `Execute()` flow. Would you take it as a PR? Happy to close if not.\n\nDisclosure: I maintain RepoLens, a docs tool, and used it (v1.15.2) for the first draft; everything was checked against the source by hand.\n\n<details><summary>Draft site/content/architecture.md</summary>\n\n# Architecture (for contributors)\n\nAll of Cobra is one Go package in the repo root; `doc/` is a separate package that generates man/markdown/rst/yaml docs. Dependencies: `spf13/pflag` (flags), `inconshreveable/mousetrap` (Windows Explorer detection) and `cpuguy83/go-md2man` (for `doc/`).\n\n| File | What it holds |\n|---|---|\n| `command.go` (~2,100 lines) | `Command`: tree building, `Execute`/`ExecuteC`, `Find`/`Traverse`, flag parsing, hooks, help/usage/version. |\n| `cobra.go` | Package globals and template functions, `OnInitialize`, `EnableCommandSorting`, etc. |\n| `args.go` | Positional-arg validators (`NoArgs`, `ExactArgs`, `MatchAll`, …). |\n| `flag_groups.go` | `MarkFlagsRequiredTogether`, `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive`, `MarkFlagsOneRequired`. |\n| `completions.go` (~1,000) | The hidden `__complete` command, `ValidArgsFunction`, and the default `completion` command. |\n| `bash_completions*.go`, `zsh_`, `fish_`, `powershell_completions.go` | Shell-specific completion script generators. |\n| `active_help.go` | Active Help messages shown during completion. |\n| `command_win.go` / `command_notwin.go` | Platform-specific pre-exec (mousetrap). |\n\n## How `Execute()` runs\n1. `Execute()` calls `ExecuteC()` on the root, which adds the default help and completion commands (`InitDefaultHelpCmd`, `InitDefaultCompletionCmd`).\n2. It finds the target with `Find(args)` (or `Traverse` when `TraverseChildren` is set).\n3. `execute()` parses flags, handles `--help`/`--version`, validates args and flag groups, then runs `PersistentPreRun` → `PreRun` → `Run` → `PostRun` → `PersistentPostRun` (the `E` variants return errors).\n\n---\n<sub>Drafted with [RepoLens](https://github.com/CHAPIBUNNY/repolens), checked by hand.</sub>\n\n</details>\n", 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'CHAPIBUNNY'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 1, 'created_at': '2026-10-21T18:55:13Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-24T08:34:14Z'}, {'number': 2544, 'title': 'Mousetrap ignores the arguments: explorer.exe-started commands with a full command line exit 1', 'body': '**The mousetrap blocks a full command line started by explorer.exe**\n\nRepro (Windows 11, cobra v1.10.2):\n1. Register a cobra CLI in Programs and Features with `UninstallString = "C:\\...\\app.exe" uninstall --purge`.\n2. Control Panel → Programs and Features → Uninstall.\n3. Explorer starts `app.exe uninstall --purge` with `explorer.exe` as the parent.\n\nCurrent:\n- cobra prints "This is a command line tool", waits 5s, exits 1.\n- The `uninstall` command never runs.\n\nExpected:\n- The mousetrap catches a double-click only.\n- A double-click passes no arguments. Explorer starts with arguments only for an explicit command line (an uninstall entry, a shortcut).\n- So: show the mousetrap only when `len(os.Args) == 1`.\n\nWhy it matters:\n- Today the only fix is `MousetrapHelpText = ""` globally, which also drops the useful double-click message.\n- Any cobra CLI with a Windows uninstall entry or shortcut with arguments hits this.\n\nRelated: #486, #619 (disable per command). This asks for a smarter default, not a new switch.\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'danikpfive'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-10-21T16:07:31Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-21T16:07:31Z'}, {'number': 2528, 'title': 'TraverseChildren can execute a subcommand after -- and discard positional arguments', 'body': '\n\n## Description\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, Cobra can interpret a token after the `--` delimiter as a subcommand and execute its handler.\n\nIn the reproduction below, `./app -- literal child` invokes `child` instead of invoking the root command with positional arguments `["literal", "child"]`. The `literal` argument is also discarded. Execution returns successfully, making the wrong-handler behavior easy to miss.\n\nThe same command tree behaves correctly with `TraverseChildren: false`.\n\n## Environment\n\n- Cobra commit: `adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e`\n- pflag: `v1.0.9`\n- OS/architecture: Linux/amd64\n- Go: `go1.27.2-X:nodwarf5`\n\n## Minimal reproduction\n\nSave as `main.go` in an empty directory:\n\n```go\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t"fmt"\n\t"os"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\troot := &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse:              "app",\n\t\tTraverseChildren: true,\n\t\tArgs:             cobra.ArbitraryArgs,\n\t\tRun: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Printf("root called with %q\\n", args)\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\troot.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse: "child",\n\t\tRun: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Println("child called")\n\t\t},\n\t})\n\tif err := root.Execute(); err != nil {\n\t\tos.Exit(1)\n\t}\n}\n```\n\nInitialize and build:\n\n```sh\ngo mod init example.com/cobra-traverse-repro\ngo get github.com/spf13/cobra@adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e\ngo build -o app .\n```\n\nRun:\n\n```sh\n./app -- literal child\n```\n\n## Actual behavior\n\n```text\nchild called\n```\n\nThe child handler runs, `literal` is discarded, and the process exits with status 0.\n\n## Expected behavior\n\n```text\nroot called with ["literal" "child"]\n```\n\nThe delimiter should stop command discovery on this path, consistent with the default `Find` path. Both subsequent tokens should remain positional arguments for the root command.\n\n## Controls\n\nChange only `TraverseChildren: true` to `TraverseChildren: false`, rebuild, and rerun the same command. It produces the expected root output.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`:\n\n```sh\n./app -- child\n# root called with ["child"]\n\n./app -- literal other\n# root called with ["literal" "other"]\n\n./app child\n# child called\n```\n\nThese controls show that the failure depends on the later positional token matching an existing subcommand after the first post-delimiter token has been consumed.\n\n## Cause\n\nIn [`Command.Traverse`](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e/command.go#L821-L857), the long-flag branch also matches a bare `--`:\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--") && !strings.Contains(arg, "="):\n    inFlag = !hasNoOptDefVal(arg[2:], c.Flags())\n    flags = append(flags, arg)\n    continue\n```\n\nFor `--`, `arg[2:]` is empty, so no flag is found and `inFlag` becomes true. The next token (`literal`) is consumed as a supposed flag value. `Traverse` then resumes command discovery, finds `child`, parses the accumulated `["--", "literal"]` on the parent, and recurses into the child with the remaining arguments. The parent\'s positional arguments are not passed to that child.\n\nThe default `stripFlags` path explicitly stops discovery on `--`, whereas this traversal path does not.\n\n## Impact and additional verification\n\nApplications using `TraverseChildren` can run an unintended command handler when positional data after `--` matches a child command name. Arguments before that match may also be lost.\n\nThe reproduction uses a fresh process and requires neither user-defined flags nor completion setup. Three repeated regression runs reproduced the failure with `TraverseChildren: true`, while the otherwise identical `false` control passed each time.\n\nUpstream `main` was checked on 2026-10-15. Its `command.go` had the same blob SHA as the tested local file: `c05fed45aef0cfed0304728c2289aa18fb152dad`.\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'aditya-rai-5'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-10-15T18:15:51Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-15T18:15:51Z'}, {'number': 2527, 'title': 'Shell completion parses flags twice, duplicating array/slice values and doubling count flags', 'body': '## Description\n\nA single `__complete` request parses the target command\'s flags twice before calling its completion callback. As a result, repeatable flag values differ between normal execution and completion:\n\n- `StringArrayVar`: one `--tag one` becomes `["one", "one"]`.\n- `StringSliceVar`: the same duplication occurs.\n- `CountVarP`: one `-v` produces `2` rather than `1`.\n\nThis occurs with a fresh command in a fresh process. I drafted a short page (proposed `site/content/architecture.md`, draft below) mapping the files and the `Execute()` flow. Would you take it as a PR? Happy to close if not.\n\nDisclosure: I maintain RepoLens, a docs tool, and used it (v1.15.2) for the first draft; everything was checked against the source by hand.\n\n<details><summary>Draft site/content/architecture.md</summary>\n\n# Architecture (for contributors)\n\nAll of Cobra is one Go package in the repo root; `doc/` is a separate package that generates man/markdown/rst/yaml docs. Dependencies: `spf13/pflag` (flags), `inconshreveable/mousetrap` (Windows Explorer detection) and `cpuguy83/go-md2man` (for `doc/`).\n\n| File | What it holds |\n|---|---|\n| `command.go` (~2,100 lines) | `Command`: tree building, `Execute`/`ExecuteC`, `Find`/`Traverse`, flag parsing, hooks, help/usage/version. |\n| `cobra.go` | Package globals and template functions, `OnInitialize`, `EnableCommandSorting`, etc. |\n| `args.go` | Positional-arg validators (`NoArgs`, `ExactArgs`, `MatchAll`, …). |\n| `flag_groups.go` | `MarkFlagsRequiredTogether`, `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive`, `MarkFlagsOneRequired`. |\n| `completions.go` (~1,000) | The hidden `__complete` command, `ValidArgsFunction`, and the default `completion` command. |\n| `bash_completions*.go`, `zsh_`, `fish_`, `powershell_completions.go` | Shell-specific completion script generators. |\n| `active_help.go` | Active Help messages shown during completion. |\n| `command_win.go` / `command_notwin.go` | Platform-specific pre-exec (mousetrap). |\n\n## How `Execute()` runs\n1. `Execute()` calls `ExecuteC()` on the root, which adds the default help and completion commands (`InitDefaultHelpCmd`, `InitDefaultCompletionCmd`).\n2. It finds the target with `Find(args)` (or `Traverse` when `TraverseChildren` is set).\n3. `execute()` parses flags, handles `--help`/`--version`, validates args and flag groups, then runs `PersistentPreRun` → `PreRun` → `Run` → `PostRun` → `PersistentPostRun` (the `E` variants return errors).\n\n---\n<sub>Drafted with [RepoLens](https://github.com/CHAPIBUNNY/repolens), checked by hand.</sub>\n\n</details>\n", 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'CHAPIBUNNY'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 1, 'created_at': '2026-10-21T18:55:13Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-24T08:34:14Z'}, {'number': 2544, 'title': 'Mousetrap ignores the arguments: explorer.exe-started commands with a full command line exit 1', 'body': '**The mousetrap blocks a full command line started by explorer.exe**\n\nRepro (Windows 11, cobra v1.10.2):\n1. Register a cobra CLI in Programs and Features with `UninstallString = "C:\\...\\app.exe" uninstall --purge`.\n2. Control Panel → Programs and Features → Uninstall.\n3. Explorer starts `app.exe uninstall --purge` with `explorer.exe` as the parent.\n\nCurrent:\n- cobra prints "This is a command line tool", waits 5s, exits 1.\n- The `uninstall` command never runs.\n\nExpected:\n- The mousetrap catches a double-click only.\n- A double-click passes no arguments. Explorer starts with arguments only for an explicit command line (an uninstall entry, a shortcut).\n- So: show the mousetrap only when `len(os.Args) == 1`.\n\nWhy it matters:\n- Today the only fix is `MousetrapHelpText = ""` globally, which also drops the useful double-click message.\n- Any cobra CLI with a Windows uninstall entry or shortcut with arguments hits this.\n\nRelated: #486, #619 (disable per command). The `literal` argument is also discarded. Execution returns successfully, making the wrong-handler behavior easy to miss.\n\nThe same command tree behaves correctly with `TraverseChildren: false`.\n\n## Environment\n\n- Cobra commit: `adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e`\n- pflag: `v1.0.9`\n- OS/architecture: Linux/amd64\n- Go: `go1.27.2-X:nodwarf5`\n\n## Minimal reproduction\n\nSave as `main.go` in an empty directory:\n\n```go\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t"fmt"\n\t"os"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\troot := &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse:              "app",\n\t\tTraverseChildren: true,\n\t\tArgs:             cobra.ArbitraryArgs,\n\t\tRun: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Printf("root called with %q\\n", args)\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\troot.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse: "child",\n\t\tRun: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Println("child called")\n\t\t},\n\t})\n\tif err := root.Execute(); err != nil {\n\t\tos.Exit(1)\n\t}\n}\n```\n\nInitialize and build:\n\n```sh\ngo mod init example.com/cobra-traverse-repro\ngo get github.com/spf13/cobra@adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e\ngo build -o app .\n```\n\nRun:\n\n```sh\n./app -- literal child\n```\n\n## Actual behavior\n\n```text\nchild called\n```\n\nThe child handler runs, `literal` is discarded, and the process exits with status 0.\n\n## Expected behavior\n\n```text\nroot called with ["literal" "child"]\n```\n\nThe delimiter should stop command discovery on this path, consistent with the default `Find` path. Both subsequent tokens should remain positional arguments for the root command.\n\n## Controls\n\nChange only `TraverseChildren: true` to `TraverseChildren: false`, rebuild, and rerun the same command. It produces the expected root output.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`:\n\n```sh\n./app -- child\n# root called with ["child"]\n\n./app -- literal other\n# root called with ["literal" "other"]\n\n./app child\n# child called\n```\n\nThese controls show that the failure depends on the later positional token matching an existing subcommand after the first post-delimiter token has been consumed.\n\n## Cause\n\nIn [`Command.Traverse`](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e/command.go#L821-L857), the long-flag branch also matches a bare `--`:\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--") && !strings.Contains(arg, "="):\n    inFlag = !hasNoOptDefVal(arg[2:], c.Flags())\n    flags = append(flags, arg)\n    continue\n```\n\nFor `--`, `arg[2:]` is empty, so no flag is found and `inFlag` becomes true. The next token (`literal`) is consumed as a supposed flag value. `Traverse` then resumes command discovery, finds `child`, parses the accumulated `["--", "literal"]` on the parent, and recurses into the child with the remaining arguments. The parent\'s positional arguments are not passed to that child.\n\nThe default `stripFlags` path explicitly stops discovery on `--`, whereas this traversal path does not.\n\n## Impact and additional verification\n\nApplications using `TraverseChildren` can run an unintended command handler when positional data after `--` matches a child command name. Arguments before that match may also be lost.\n\nThe reproduction uses a fresh process and requires neither user-defined flags nor completion setup. Three repeated regression runs reproduced the failure with `TraverseChildren: true`, while the otherwise identical `false` control passed each time.\n\nUpstream `main` was checked on 2026-10-15.
