'title': 'fix: treat lone dash as positional during command discovery', 'body': 'When a runnable root command accepts positional arguments and has a `child` subcommand, `root - child` currently executes `child` with `-` as its argument. Replacing `-` with an ordinary filename keeps execution on the root. Enabling `TraverseChildren` also keeps the lone dash on the root, consistent with pflag treating `-` as a positional argument.\n\nUse the existing `isFlagArg` predicate in command discovery and matched-command removal. A lone dash can then stop subcommand discovery like other positional arguments. If an application explicitly defines `-` as a command name or alias, its command token is removed normally. Flag values and the `--` terminator retain their existing handling.\n\nValidation on macOS arm64 with Go 1.25.3:\n\n- The strip-flags case and default-dispatch regressions failed before the fix.\n- Added coverage for lone dashes before and after a subcommand, after a boolean flag, as a flag value, around `--`, and as a command name or alias.\n- `go test ./...` passes.\n- `make all` (formatting and full tests) and `git diff --check` pass. The optional golangci-lint binary is not installed locally.\n\nAI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped implement and test this change.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'ibrahimypr', 'state': 'closed', 'locked': False, 'title': 'fix: prevent completions from mutating os.Args via append side effect', 'body': '## Summary\n\n- Fixes a bug where `getCompletions()` accidentally mutates `os.Args` by writing `"--"` into the shared backing array via an `append` with spare capacity\n- Uses a three-index slice expression (`finalArgs[:len:len]`) to cap the slice capacity, forcing `append` to allocate a new array\n- Adds a regression test that confirms the args slice is not corrupted during shell completion\n\n## Details\n\nWhen shell completions are requested (e.g., `prog __complete x`), `getCompletions()` calls:\n\n```go\n_ = finalCmd.ParseFlags(append(finalArgs, "--"))\n```\n\n`finalArgs` is a sub-slice of the original args (derived from `os.Args[1:]`), and if it has spare capacity in its backing array, `append` writes `"--"` directly into the shared memory rather than allocating a new slice. This corrupts `os.Args`, which users may be inspecting in their `ValidArgsFunction`.\n\nThe fix uses `finalArgs[:len(finalArgs):len(finalArgs)]` to limit the capacity to the length, guaranteeing that `append` allocates a fresh backing array.\n\nThe bug is most visible with `TraverseChildren: true`, since `Traverse()` returns sub-slices that preserve the original backing array\'s capacity.\n\nFixes #2257\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] Added `TestCompletionDoesNotMutateArgs` that fails without the fix and passes with it\n- [x] Full test suite passes (`go test ./...`)', 'author_association': 'title': "command: stop Traverse at `--` so a positional isn't run as a subcommand", 'body': '## Bug (fixes #2528)\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, the long-flag branch of `Command.Traverse` matched a bare `--` as a flag that "takes a value":\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--") && !strings.Contains(arg, "="):\n    inFlag = !hasNoOptDefVal(arg[2:], c.Flags())\n    flags = append(flags, arg)\n    continue\n```\n\n`arg[2:]` is `""`, no flag by that name exists, so `inFlag = true`. The next positional is consumed as that flag\'s "value" and the following positional happens to match a subcommand — so the child handler runs, the first post-`--` positional is silently dropped, and the parent\'s positionals never reach any command.\n\nReproduction from the issue:\n\n```go\nroot := &cobra.Command{Use:"app", TraverseChildren:true, Args:cobra.ArbitraryArgs,\n    Run: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string){ fmt.Printf("root called with %q\\\\n", args) }}\nroot.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{Use:"child",\n    Run: func(*cobra.Command, []string){ fmt.Println("child called") }})\nroot.Execute()\n```\n\n```\n$ ./app -- literal child\nchild called                 # bug: wrong handler, "literal" lost\n$ # expected:\nroot called with ["literal" "child"]\n```\n\nThe default (non-traverse) `stripFlags` path already stops command discovery on `--`.\n\n## Fix\n\nMirror that behaviour. When `Traverse` sees a bare `--`:\n\n1. Parse any flags accumulated so far on the current command.\n2. Return the current command along with the remaining args starting at the delimiter, so a downstream parser sees the exact slice it would have gotten without `TraverseChildren`.\n\n## Test\n\n`TestTraverseStopsAtEndOfFlags` covers two cases:\n\n- `[]string{"--", "literal", "child"}` → traversal stays on root, remaining is unchanged.\n- `[]string{"--", "child"}` → traversal stays on 'title': 'fix: stop Traverse command discovery at bare --', 'body': '## Description\n\nFixes #2528.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, `Command.Traverse` treated a bare `--` as a long flag with an empty name (`arg[2:] == ""`). The next token was consumed as that flag\'s value, then command discovery resumed, so `./app -- literal child` could execute `child` and drop `literal`.\n\n`stripFlags` / `Find` already stop at `--`. Traverse now does the same: when it sees a bare `--` (and is not already collecting a flag value), it returns the current command with the full args for that level so `Execute` parses flags once and keeps later tokens as positionals.\n\n## Checklist\n\n- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).\n- [x] The code has adequate tests for the new feature / bug.\n- [x] Tests pass: `go test -run TestTraverse .`\n\n## Testing\n\n- New: `TestTraverseBareDoubleDashStopsCommandDiscovery` (`-- literal child`, `-- child`, and plain `child` controls).\n- Existing `TestTraverse*` suite passed locally.\n\n## AI assistance\n\nAI tools helped draft the patch, tests, and PR text. I reviewed the change, ran the tests above, and take responsibility for the contents.', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'user_view_type': 'public', 2510, 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': "Handle combined shorthands in Traverse's value-flag detection", 'body': '## `Traverse` mishandles a combined shorthand cluster that ends in a value flag\n\n### Description\n\n`command.go`, in `Traverse`, the "short flag with a space separated value" case:\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n    inFlag = true\n```\n\n`len(arg) == 2` recognises only a **single** shorthand. A combined cluster such as `-ab` (where `-a` is a bool and `-b` takes a value) is mis-handled: `Traverse` appends `-ab` to `flags` **without** setting `inFlag`, so the following argument is looked up as a **subcommand name**.\n\n### Why it\'s wrong\n\npflag\'s real rule — verified directly with `pflag parse [-ab sub2] err=<nil> args=[] all=true bind="sub2"` — is that the first shorthand lacking a `NoOptDefVal` swallows the rest of the cluster, and only reaches into the next argv slot when it is the *last* shorthand. Cobra must predict that split in order to locate the target command, and for clusters it predicts wrong.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, `prog child -ab grandchild` fails with:\n\n```\nflag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n```\n\neven though the value *was* supplied — and the equivalent `prog child -a -b grandchild` works. Valid input is rejected with a misleading error.\n\n### Upstream status\n\n- Issue **#2188** ("Combining shorthand flags before command names does not work") is open but is about flags *before* the command name (`mycli -C elephant first second`).\n- PR **#2189** ("Fix shorthand combination edge case") is open and unmerged, and its diff touches only `stripFlags` / `argsMinusFirstX` / `Find` — it does **not** touch `Traverse`, so the `TraverseChildren: true` path is unfixed by any open PR.\n\n## The fix\n\n```go\n// shortCombinationTakesNextArg reports whether the value of a single dash\n// shorthand argument (such as "-a" or "-ab") is taken from the following\n// argument, rather than being embedded in the argument itself.\n//\n// This mirrors how pflag parses shorthand arguments: the first shorthand of the\n// combination that does not have a NoOptDefVal consumes the remainder of the\n// combination as its value, and it only reaches out to the next argument when\n// that shorthand is the last one of the combination. So "-ab value" consumes\n// "value" for -b (when -a is a boolean), while "-bvalue" does not.\nfunc shortCombinationTakesNextArg(combination string, fs *flag.FlagSet) bool {\n\tlast := len(combination) - 1\n\tfor i := 0; i <= last; i++ {\n\t\tif !shortHasNoOptDefVal(combination[i:i+1], fs) {\n\t\t\t// This shorthand needs a value. It only comes from the next argument\n\t\t\t// if the combination ends here.\n\t\t\treturn i == last\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n```\n\nand in `Traverse`:\n\n```diff\n-\t\tcase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n+\t\tcase len(arg) > 1 && strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") &&\n+\t\t\tshortCombinationTakesNextArg(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n```\n\nThe `len(arg) > 1` guard is load-bearing: without it a bare `-` (which pflag treats as a positional argument) would start matching and get appended to `flags`.\n\n## Tests\n\n`TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue` (6 subtests) and `TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue`, both added to `command_test.go`.\n\n- Before:\n  ```\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_a_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_an_inherited_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'C\' in -C\n  --- FAIL: TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue\n      command_test.go:2543: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  ```\n  After: all pass.\n- Four control subtests (`value_inside_the_cluster`, `all_boolean_cluster`, `single_value_flag`, `single_bool_flag`) pass **both** before and after, proving the fix does not over-consume arguments.\n- `go test ./...`: root package **404 → 412 PASS** (+8), `cobra/doc` 19 PASS, **0 failures**. Baseline on unmodified HEAD was fully green with zero pre-existing failures. `go vet ./...` clean.\n\nThe 36 `gofmt -l` hits are a pre-existing repo-wide CRLF artefact of this Windows checkout — identical count before and after, so this change adds none.\n\n## Note\n\nThis repository asks contributors to sign a CLA; I have not done so, since that is a legal attestation only the contributor can make.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'januththedev', 'id': 96273863, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'U_kgDOBb0Fxw', 'avatar_url': 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': 'Provide usefull errors when using invalid sub command', 'body': "If the *TraverseChildren* mode is active, the *Traverse* function returns the last accepted command along the requested sub command chain. This command is then used to parse the arguments. This will for sure fail, if the traversing was aborted because an invalid sub command was given. As a result, cobra complains about invalid flags instead of an invalid sub command.\r\n\r\nThis behaviour might be useful, if the intermediate command is *Runnable()*, but it for sure makes no sense, if it isn't.\r\n\r\nThis PR fixes this by providing a *legacyArgs()* error in case of not runnable intermediate commands.\r\n\r\n---\r\n*Remark:* It solves the obvious problematic behaviour, but basically the general scenario is more complex.\r\nIf the intermediate command is *Runnable()* in addition to providing additional sub commands, then it should be possible to forward the control about the error message to the command to be a able to distinguish between these two cases according to its needs. This is basically already possible by declaring a *FlagErrorFunc()*. But unfortunately it only gets the command and error as arguments, but not the actual set of arguments. Therefore it has no chance to detect the actual problem and provide appropriate error feedback.\r\n\r\nSolving this is more invasive, because it would require, either to change the interface, or add another more general error handler option.\r\n\r\n", 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'mandelsoft', 'id': 553075, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'MDQ6VXNlcjU1MzA3NQ==', 'title': 'fix: treat lone dash as positional during command discovery', 'body': 'When a runnable root command accepts positional arguments and has a `child` subcommand, `root - child` currently executes `child` with `-` as its argument. Replacing `-` with an ordinary filename keeps execution on the root. Enabling `TraverseChildren` also keeps the lone dash on the root, consistent with pflag treating `-` as a positional argument.\n\nUse the existing `isFlagArg` predicate in command discovery and matched-command removal. A lone dash can then stop subcommand discovery like other positional arguments. If an application explicitly defines `-` as a command name or alias, its command token is removed normally. Flag values and the `--` terminator retain their existing handling.\n\nValidation on macOS arm64 with Go 1.25.3:\n\n- The strip-flags case and default-dispatch regressions failed before the fix.\n- Added coverage for lone dashes before and after a subcommand, after a boolean flag, as a flag value, around `--`, and as a command name or alias.\n- `go test ./...` passes.\n- `make all` (formatting and full tests) and `git diff --check` pass. The optional golangci-lint binary is not installed locally.\n\nAI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped implement and test this change.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'ibrahimypr', 'state': 'closed', 'locked': False, 'title': 'fix: prevent completions from mutating os.Args via append side effect', 'body': '## Summary\n\n- Fixes a bug where `getCompletions()` accidentally mutates `os.Args` by writing `"--"` into the shared backing array via an `append` with spare capacity\n- Uses a three-index slice expression (`finalArgs[:len:len]`) to cap the slice capacity, forcing `append` to allocate a new array\n- Adds a regression test that confirms the args slice is not corrupted during shell completion\n\n## Details\n\nWhen shell completions are requested (e.g., `prog __complete x`), `getCompletions()` calls:\n\n```go\n_ = finalCmd.ParseFlags(append(finalArgs, "--"))\n```\n\n`finalArgs` is a sub-slice of the original args (derived from `os.Args[1:]`), and if it has spare capacity in its backing array, `append` writes `"--"` directly into the shared memory rather than allocating a new slice. This corrupts `os.Args`, which users may be inspecting in their `ValidArgsFunction`.\n\nThe fix uses `finalArgs[:len(finalArgs):len(finalArgs)]` to limit the capacity to the length, guaranteeing that `append` allocates a fresh backing array.\n\nThe bug is most visible with `TraverseChildren: true`, since `Traverse()` returns sub-slices that preserve the original backing array\'s capacity.\n\nFixes #2257\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] Added `TestCompletionDoesNotMutateArgs` that fails without the fix and passes with it\n- [x] Full test suite passes (`go test ./...`)', 'author_association': 2510, 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': "Handle combined shorthands in Traverse's value-flag detection", 'body': '## `Traverse` mishandles a combined shorthand cluster that ends in a value flag\n\n### Description\n\n`command.go`, in `Traverse`, the "short flag with a space separated value" case:\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n    inFlag = true\n```\n\n`len(arg) == 2` recognises only a **single** shorthand. A combined cluster such as `-ab` (where `-a` is a bool and `-b` takes a value) is mis-handled: `Traverse` appends `-ab` to `flags` **without** setting `inFlag`, so the following argument is looked up as a **subcommand name**.\n\n### Why it\'s wrong\n\npflag\'s real rule — verified directly with `pflag parse [-ab sub2] err=<nil> args=[] all=true bind="sub2"` — is that the first shorthand lacking a `NoOptDefVal` swallows the rest of the cluster, and only reaches into the next argv slot when it is the *last* shorthand. Cobra must predict that split in order to locate the target command, and for clusters it predicts wrong.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, `prog child -ab grandchild` fails with:\n\n```\nflag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n```\n\neven though the value *was* supplied — and the equivalent `prog child -a -b grandchild` works. Valid input is rejected with a misleading error.\n\n### Upstream status\n\n- Issue **#2188** ("Combining shorthand flags before command names does not work") is open but is about flags *before* the command name (`mycli -C elephant first second`).\n- PR **#2189** ("Fix shorthand combination edge case") is open and unmerged, and its diff touches only `stripFlags` / `argsMinusFirstX` / `Find` — it does **not** touch `Traverse`, so the `TraverseChildren: true` path is unfixed by any open PR.\n\n## The fix\n\n```go\n// shortCombinationTakesNextArg reports whether the value of a single dash\n// shorthand argument (such as "-a" or "-ab") is taken from the following\n// argument, rather than being embedded in the argument itself.\n//\n// This mirrors how pflag parses shorthand arguments: the first shorthand of the\n// combination that does not have a NoOptDefVal consumes the remainder of the\n// combination as its value, and it only reaches out to the next argument when\n// that shorthand is the last one of the combination. So "-ab value" consumes\n// "value" for -b (when -a is a boolean), while "-bvalue" does not.\nfunc shortCombinationTakesNextArg(combination string, fs *flag.FlagSet) bool {\n\tlast := len(combination) - 1\n\tfor i := 0; i <= last; i++ {\n\t\tif !shortHasNoOptDefVal(combination[i:i+1], fs) {\n\t\t\t// This shorthand needs a value. It only comes from the next argument\n\t\t\t// if the combination ends here.\n\t\t\treturn i == last\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n```\n\nand in `Traverse`:\n\n```diff\n-\t\tcase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n+\t\tcase len(arg) > 1 && strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") &&\n+\t\t\tshortCombinationTakesNextArg(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n```\n\nThe `len(arg) > 1` guard is load-bearing: without it a bare `-` (which pflag treats as a positional argument) would start matching and get appended to `flags`.\n\n## Tests\n\n`TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue` (6 subtests) and `TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue`, both added to `command_test.go`.\n\n- Before:\n  ```\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_a_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_an_inherited_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'C\' in -C\n  --- FAIL: TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue\n      command_test.go:2543: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  ```\n  After: all pass.\n- Four control subtests (`value_inside_the_cluster`, `all_boolean_cluster`, `single_value_flag`, `single_bool_flag`) pass **both** before and after, proving the fix does not over-consume arguments.\n- `go test ./...`: root package **404 → 412 PASS** (+8), `cobra/doc` 19 PASS, **0 failures**. Baseline on unmodified HEAD was fully green with zero pre-existing failures. `go vet ./...` clean.\n\nThe 36 `gofmt -l` hits are a pre-existing repo-wide CRLF artefact of this Windows checkout — identical count before and after, so this change adds none.\n\n## Note\n\nThis repository asks contributors to sign a CLA; I have not done so, since that is a legal attestation only the contributor 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': 'Provide usefull errors when using invalid sub command', 'body': "If the *TraverseChildren* mode is active, the *Traverse* function returns the last accepted command along the requested sub command chain. This command is then used to parse the arguments. This will for sure fail, if the traversing was aborted because an invalid sub command was given. As a result, cobra complains about invalid flags instead of an invalid sub command.\r\n\r\nThis behaviour might be useful, if the intermediate command is *Runnable()*, but it for sure makes no sense, if it isn't.\r\n\r\nThis PR fixes this by providing a *legacyArgs()* error in case of not runnable intermediate commands.\r\n\r\n---\r\n*Remark:* It solves the obvious problematic behaviour, but basically the general scenario is more complex.\r\nIf the intermediate command is *Runnable()* in addition to providing additional sub commands, then it should be possible to forward the control about the error message to the command to be a able to distinguish between these two cases according to its needs. This is basically already possible by declaring a *FlagErrorFunc()*. But unfortunately it only gets the command and error as arguments, but not the actual set of arguments. Therefore it has no chance to detect the actual problem and provide appropriate error feedback.\r\n\r\nSolving this is more invasive, because it would require, either to change the interface, or add another more general error handler option.\r\n\r\n", 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'mandelsoft', 'id': 553075, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'MDQ6VXNlcjU1MzA3NQ==', 'title': 'fix: treat lone dash as positional during command discovery', 'body': 'When a runnable root command accepts positional arguments and has a `child` subcommand, `root - child` currently executes `child` with `-` as its argument. Replacing `-` with an ordinary filename keeps execution on the root. Enabling `TraverseChildren` also keeps the lone dash on the root, consistent with pflag treating `-` as a positional argument.\n\nUse the existing `isFlagArg` predicate in command discovery and matched-command removal. A lone dash can then stop subcommand discovery like other positional arguments. If an application explicitly defines `-` as a command name or alias, its command token is removed normally. Flag values and the `--` terminator retain their existing handling.\n\nValidation on macOS arm64 with Go 1.25.3:\n\n- The strip-flags case and default-dispatch regressions failed before the fix.\n- Added coverage for lone dashes before and after a subcommand, after a boolean flag, as a flag value, around `--`, and as a command name or alias.\n- `go test ./...` passes.\n- `make all` (formatting and full tests) and `git diff --check` pass. The optional golangci-lint binary is not installed locally.\n\nAI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped implement and test this change.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'ibrahimypr', 'state': 'closed', 'locked': False, 'title': 'fix: prevent completions from mutating os.Args via append side effect', 'body': '## Summary\n\n- Fixes a bug where `getCompletions()` accidentally mutates `os.Args` by writing `"--"` into the shared backing array via an `append` with spare capacity\n- Uses a three-index slice expression (`finalArgs[:len:len]`) to cap the slice capacity, forcing `append` to allocate a new array\n- Adds a regression test that confirms the args slice is not corrupted during shell completion\n\n## Details\n\nWhen shell completions are requested (e.g., `prog __complete x`), `getCompletions()` calls:\n\n```go\n_ = finalCmd.ParseFlags(append(finalArgs, "--"))\n```\n\n`finalArgs` is a sub-slice of the original args (derived from `os.Args[1:]`), and if it has spare capacity in its backing array, `append` writes `"--"` directly into the shared memory rather than allocating a new slice. This corrupts `os.Args`, which users may be inspecting in their `ValidArgsFunction`.\n\nThe fix uses `finalArgs[:len(finalArgs):len(finalArgs)]` to limit the capacity to the length, guaranteeing that `append` allocates a fresh backing array.\n\nThe bug is most visible with `TraverseChildren: true`, since `Traverse()` returns sub-slices that preserve the original backing array\'s capacity.\n\nFixes 'title': "command: stop Traverse at `--` so a positional isn't run as a subcommand", 'body': '## Bug (fixes #2528)\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, the long-flag branch of `Command.Traverse` matched a bare `--` as a flag that "takes a value":\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--") && !strings.Contains(arg, "="):\n    inFlag = !hasNoOptDefVal(arg[2:], c.Flags())\n    flags = append(flags, arg)\n    continue\n```\n\n`arg[2:]` is `""`, no flag by that name exists, so `inFlag = true`. The next positional is consumed as that flag\'s "value" and the following positional happens to match a subcommand — so the child handler runs, the first post-`--` positional is silently dropped, and the parent\'s positionals never reach any command.\n\nReproduction from the issue:\n\n```go\nroot := &cobra.Command{Use:"app", TraverseChildren:true, Args:cobra.ArbitraryArgs,\n    Run: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string){ fmt.Printf("root called with %q\\\\n", args) }}\nroot.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{Use:"child",\n    Run: func(*cobra.Command, []string){ fmt.Println("child called") }})\nroot.Execute()\n```\n\n```\n$ ./app -- literal child\nchild called                 # bug: wrong handler, "literal" lost\n$ # expected:\nroot called with ["literal" "child"]\n```\n\nThe default (non-traverse) `stripFlags` path already stops command discovery on `--`.\n\n## Fix\n\nMirror that behaviour. When `Traverse` sees a bare `--`:\n\n1. Parse any flags accumulated so far on the current command.\n2. Return the current command along with the remaining args starting at the delimiter, so a downstream parser sees the exact slice it would have gotten without `TraverseChildren`.\n\n## empty name (`arg[2:] == ""`). Traverse now does the same: when it sees a bare `--` (and is not already collecting a flag value), it returns the current command with the full args for that level so `Execute` parses flags once and keeps later tokens as positionals.\n\n## Checklist\n\n- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).\n- [x] The code has adequate tests for the new feature / bug.\n- [x] Tests pass: `go test -run TestTraverse .`\n\n## Testing\n\n- New: `TestTraverseBareDoubleDashStopsCommandDiscovery` (`-- literal child`, `-- child`, and plain `child` controls).\n- Existing `TestTraverse*` suite passed locally.\n\n## AI assistance\n\nAI tools helped draft the patch, tests, and PR text. 2510, 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': "Handle combined shorthands in Traverse's value-flag detection", 'body': '## `Traverse` mishandles a combined shorthand cluster that ends in a value flag\n\n### Description\n\n`command.go`, in `Traverse`, the "short flag with a space separated value" case:\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n    inFlag = true\n```\n\n`len(arg) == 2` recognises only a **single** shorthand. A combined cluster such as `-ab` (where `-a` is a bool and `-b` takes a value) is mis-handled: `Traverse` appends `-ab` to `flags` **without** setting `inFlag`, so the following argument is looked up as a **subcommand name**.\n\n### Why it\'s wrong\n\npflag\'s real rule — verified directly with `pflag parse [-ab sub2] err=<nil> args=[] all=true bind="sub2"` — is that the first shorthand lacking a `NoOptDefVal` swallows the rest of the cluster, and only reaches into the next argv slot when it is the *last* shorthand. Cobra must predict that split in order to locate the target command, and for clusters it predicts wrong.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, `prog child -ab grandchild` fails with:\n\n```\nflag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n```\n\neven though the value *was* supplied — and the equivalent `prog child -a -b grandchild` works. Valid input is rejected with a misleading error.\n\n### Upstream status\n\n- Issue **#2188** ("Combining shorthand flags before command names does not work") is open but is about flags *before* the command name (`mycli -C elephant first second`).\n- PR **#2189** ("Fix shorthand combination edge case") is open and unmerged, and its diff touches only `stripFlags` / `argsMinusFirstX` / `Find` — it does **not** touch `Traverse`, so the `TraverseChildren: true` path is unfixed by any open PR.\n\n## The fix\n\n```go\n// shortCombinationTakesNextArg reports whether the value of a single dash\n// shorthand argument (such as "-a" or "-ab") is taken from the following\n// argument, rather than being embedded in the argument itself.\n//\n// This mirrors how pflag parses shorthand arguments: the first shorthand of the\n// combination that does not have a NoOptDefVal consumes the remainder of the\n// combination as its value, and it only reaches out to the next argument when\n// that shorthand is the last one of the combination. So "-ab value" consumes\n// "value" for -b (when -a is a boolean), while "-bvalue" does not.\nfunc shortCombinationTakesNextArg(combination string, fs *flag.FlagSet) bool {\n\tlast := len(combination) - 1\n\tfor i := 0; i <= last; i++ {\n\t\tif !shortHasNoOptDefVal(combination[i:i+1], fs) {\n\t\t\t// This shorthand needs a value. It only comes from the next argument\n\t\t\t// if the combination ends here.\n\t\t\treturn i == last\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n```\n\nand in `Traverse`:\n\n```diff\n-\t\tcase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n+\t\tcase len(arg) > 1 && strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") &&\n+\t\t\tshortCombinationTakesNextArg(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n```\n\nThe `len(arg) > 1` guard is load-bearing: without it a bare `-` (which pflag treats as a positional argument) would start matching and get appended to `flags`.\n\n## Tests\n\n`TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue` (6 subtests) and `TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue`, both added to `command_test.go`.\n\n- Before:\n  ```\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_a_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_an_inherited_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'C\' in -C\n  --- FAIL: TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue\n      command_test.go:2543: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  ```\n  After: all pass.\n- Four control subtests (`value_inside_the_cluster`, `all_boolean_cluster`, `single_value_flag`, `single_bool_flag`) pass **both** before and after, proving the fix does not over-consume arguments.\n- `go test ./...`: root package **404 → 412 PASS** (+8), `cobra/doc` 19 PASS, **0 failures**. Baseline on unmodified HEAD was fully green with zero pre-existing failures. `go vet ./...` clean.\n\nThe 36 `gofmt -l` hits are a pre-existing repo-wide CRLF artefact of this Windows checkout — identical count before and after, so this change adds none.\n\n## Note\n\nThis repository asks contributors to sign a CLA; I have not done so, since that is a legal attestation only the contributor can make.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'januththedev', 'id': 96273863, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'U_kgDOBb0Fxw', 'avatar_url': 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': 'Provide usefull errors when using invalid sub command', 'body': "If the *TraverseChildren* mode is active, the *Traverse* function returns the last accepted command along the requested sub command chain. This command is then used to parse the arguments. This will for sure fail, if the traversing was aborted because an invalid sub command was given. As a result, cobra complains about invalid flags instead of an invalid sub command.\r\n\r\nThis behaviour might be useful, if the intermediate command is *Runnable()*, but it for sure makes no sense, if it isn't.\r\n\r\nThis PR fixes this by providing a *legacyArgs()* error in case of not runnable intermediate commands.\r\n\r\n---\r\n*Remark:* It solves the obvious problematic behaviour, but basically the general scenario is more complex.\r\nIf the intermediate command is *Runnable()* in addition to providing additional sub commands, then it should be possible to forward the control about the error message to the command to be a able to distinguish between these two cases according to its needs. This is basically already possible by declaring a *FlagErrorFunc()*. But unfortunately it only gets the command and error as arguments, but not the actual set of arguments. Therefore it has no chance to detect the actual problem and provide appropriate error feedback.\r\n\r\nSolving this is more invasive, because it would require, either to change the interface, or add another more general error handler option.\r\n\r\n", 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'mandelsoft', 'id': 553075, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'MDQ6VXNlcjU1MzA3NQ==', 'title': 'fix: treat lone dash as positional during command discovery', 'body': 'When a runnable root command accepts positional arguments and has a `child` subcommand, `root - child` currently executes `child` with `-` as its argument. Replacing `-` with an ordinary filename keeps execution on the root. Enabling `TraverseChildren` also keeps the lone dash on the root, consistent with pflag treating `-` as a positional argument.\n\nUse the existing `isFlagArg` predicate in command discovery and matched-command removal. A lone dash can then stop subcommand discovery like other positional arguments. If an application explicitly defines `-` as a command name or alias, its command token is removed normally. Flag values and the `--` terminator retain their existing handling.\n\nValidation on macOS arm64 with Go 1.25.3:\n\n- The strip-flags case and default-dispatch regressions failed before the fix.\n- Added coverage for lone dashes before and after a subcommand, after a boolean flag, as a flag value, around `--`, and as a command name or alias.\n- `go test ./...` passes.\n- `make all` (formatting and full tests) and `git diff --check` pass. The optional golangci-lint binary is not installed locally.\n\nAI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped implement and test this change.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'ibrahimypr', 'state': 'closed', 'locked': False, 'title': 'fix: prevent completions from mutating os.Args via append side effect', 'body': '## Summary\n\n- Fixes a bug where `getCompletions()` accidentally mutates `os.Args` by writing `"--"` into the shared backing array via an `append` with spare capacity\n- Uses a three-index slice expression (`finalArgs[:len:len]`) to cap the slice capacity, forcing `append` to allocate a new array\n- Adds a regression test that confirms the args slice is not corrupted during shell completion\n\n## Details\n\nWhen shell completions are requested (e.g., `prog __complete x`), `getCompletions()` calls:\n\n```go\n_ = finalCmd.ParseFlags(append(finalArgs, "--"))\n```\n\n`finalArgs` is a sub-slice of the original args (derived from `os.Args[1:]`), and if it has spare capacity in its backing array, `append` writes `"--"` directly into the shared memory rather than allocating a new slice. This corrupts `os.Args`, which users may be inspecting in their `ValidArgsFunction`.\n\nThe fix uses `finalArgs[:len(finalArgs):len(finalArgs)]` to limit the capacity to the length, guaranteeing that `append` allocates a fresh backing array.\n\nThe bug is most visible with `TraverseChildren: true`, since `Traverse()` returns sub-slices that preserve the original backing array\'s capacity.\n\nFixes #2257\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] Added `TestCompletionDoesNotMutateArgs` that fails without the fix and passes with it\n- [x] Full test suite passes (`go test ./...`)', 'author_association': Pull request #2545 in `spf13/cobra` changed **3 files**:

| File | Status | Additions | Deletions |
|------|--------|-----------|-----------|
| `cobra.go` | modified | +2 | -2 |
| `command_win.go` | modified | +7 | -1 |
| `command_win_test.go` | added | +51 | 0 |

**Summary of changes:**

This PR refined the Windows "mousetrap" behavior so that the help message only appears when the CLI is started from Windows Explorer **with no arguments** (i.e., a double-click). Previously, it would also trigger when launched from Explorer with arguments.

- **`cobra.go`**: Updated two doc comments to clarify the Explorer-with-no-arguments condition.
- **`command_win.go`**: Extracted the mousetrap logic into a new `mousetrapApplies()` function that checks three conditions: `MousetrapHelpText` is non-empty, only one argument (the program itself), and the process was started by Explorer. Also introduced a variable `startedByExplorer` to make the function testable.
- **`command_win_test.go`** (new): Added tests covering four scenarios — double-clicked, Explorer with arguments, not from Explorer, and mousetrap disabled.

['successfully downloaded text file (SHA: 8416275f48ee051b7a6383fd87d660e796ef28f7)', '<div align="center">\n<a href="https://cobra.dev">\n<img width="512" height="535" alt="cobra-logo" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8bf9aad-b5ae-41d3-8899-d83baec10af8" />\n</a>\n</div>\n\nCobra is a library for creating powerful modern CLI applications.\n\n<a href="https://cobra.dev">Visit Cobra.dev for extensive documentation</a> \n\n\nCobra is used in many Go projects such as [Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io/),\n[Hugo](https://gohugo.io), and [GitHub CLI](https://github.com/cli/cli) to\nname a few. Cobra.\n\n[![](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/spf13/cobra/test.yml?branch=main&longCache=true&label=Test&logo=github%20actions&logoColor=fff)](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/actions?query=workflow%3ATest)\n[![Go align="center" markdown="1">\n   <sup>Supported by:</sup>\n   <br>\n   <br>\n   <a href="https://www.warp.dev/cobra">\n      <img alt="Warp sponsorship" width="400" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab8dd143-b0fd-4904-bdc5-dd7ecac94eae">\n   </a>\n\n### [Warp, the AI terminal for devs](https://www.warp.dev/cobra)\n[Try Cobra in Warp today](https://www.warp.dev/cobra)<br>\n\n</div>\n<hr>\n\n# Overview\n\nCobra is a library providing a simple interface to create powerful modern CLI\ninterfaces similar to git & go tools.\n\nCobra provides:\n* Easy subcommand-based CLIs: `app server`, `app fetch`, etc.\n* Fully POSIX-compliant flags (including short & long versions)\n* Nested subcommands\n* Global, local and cascading flags\n* Intelligent suggestions (`app srver`... did you mean `app server`?)\n* Automatic help generation for commands and flags\n* Grouping help for subcommands\n* Automatic help flag recognition of `-h`, `--help`, etc.\n* Automatically generated shell autocomplete for your application (bash, zsh, fish, powershell)\n* Automatically generated man pages for your application\n* Command aliases so you can change things without breaking them\n* The flexibility to define your own help, usage, etc.\n* Optional seamless integration with [viper](https://github.com/spf13/viper) for 12-factor apps\n\n# Concepts\n\nCobra is built on a structure of commands, arguments & flags.\n\n**Commands** represent actions, **Args** are things and **Flags** are modifiers for those actions.\n\nThe best applications read like sentences when used, and as a result, users\nintuitively know how to interact with them.\n\nThe pattern to follow is\n`APPNAME VERB NOUN --ADJECTIVE`\n    or\n`APPNAME COMMAND ARG --FLAG`.\n\nA few good real world examples may better illustrate this point.\n\nIn the following example, \'server\' is a command, and \'port\' is a flag:\n\n    hugo server --port=1313\n\nIn this command we are telling Git to clone the url bare.\n\n    git clone URL --bare\n\n## Commands\n\nCommand is the central point of the application. Each interaction that\nthe application supports will be contained in a Command. A command can\nhave children commands and optionally run an action.\n\nIn the example above, \'server\' is the command.\n\n[More about cobra.Command](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/spf13/cobra#Command)\n\n## Flags\n\nA flag is a way to modify the behavior of a command. Cobra supports\nfully POSIX-compliant flags as well as the Go [flag package](https://golang.org/pkg/flag/).\nA Cobra command can define flags that persist through to children commands\nand flags that are only available to that command.\n\nIn the example above, \'port\' is the flag.\n\nFlag functionality is provided by the [pflag\nlibrary](https://github.com/spf13/pflag), a fork of the flag standard library\nwhich maintains the same interface while adding POSIX compliance.\n\n# Installing\nUsing Cobra is easy. First, use `go get` to install the latest version\nof the library.\n\n```\ngo get -u github.com/spf13/cobra@latest\n```\n\nNext, include Cobra in your application:\n\n```go\nimport "github.com/spf13/cobra"\n```\n\n# Usage\n`cobra-cli` is a command line program to generate cobra applications and command files.\nIt will bootstrap your application scaffolding to rapidly\ndevelop a Cobra-based application. It is the easiest way to incorporate Cobra into your application.\n\nIt can be installed by running:\n\n```\ngo install github.com/spf13/cobra-cli@latest\n```\n\nFor complete details on using the Cobra-CLI generator, please read [The Cobra Generator README](https://github.com/spf13/cobra-cli/blob/main/README.md)\n\nFor complete details on using the Cobra library, please read [The Cobra User Guide](site/content/user_guide.md).\n\n# License\n\nCobra is released under the Apache 2.0 license.
